title: Specific Technique for Assessing Dyspnea
recommendation_text: Use the modified Borg scale (0-10) to assess dyspnea by asking: 'On a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 is no breathlessness and 10 is the worst breathlessness imaginable, how would you rate your breathing right now?' Document the score and compare to previous ratings to evaluate treatment effectiveness.
implementation_guidance: Assess at rest and with activity. Use a visual scale with descriptors. Document scores in a consistent location in the EHR. Implement oxygen assessment for scores ≥5.
expected_outcomes: More accurate assessment of dyspnea severity, improved titration of respiratory treatments, and better documentation of symptom progression or improvement.
target_population: Patients with respiratory conditions, particularly COPD, asthma, heart failure, or interstitial lung disease
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for improved symptom management and reduced emergency visits.
citation_authors: Kendrick KR, Baxi SC, Smith RM
citation_title: Usefulness of the modified 0-10 Borg scale in assessing the degree of dyspnea in patients with COPD and asthma

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Side Effects
recommendation_text: Ask patients these specific questions about medication side effects: 1) 'Since starting this medication, have you noticed any new symptoms or problems?' 2) 'Have you changed how you take this medication because of any side effects?' 3) 'Are there any side effects that concern you enough to consider stopping the medication?' Document responses and address concerns immediately.
implementation_guidance: Ask during medication reviews and follow-up visits. Use open-ended questions first, followed by specific questions about common side effects of each medication. Document side effects reported and actions taken.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25-30% more medication side effects, improved patient satisfaction with medication management, and reduced self-discontinuation of medications.
target_population: All patients on prescription medications, particularly those newly started on medications with significant side effect profiles
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for improved medication adherence and early identification of adverse effects.
citation_authors: Basch E, Deal AM, Kris MG, et al.
citation_title: Symptom Monitoring With Patient-Reported Outcomes During Routine Cancer Treatment: A Randomized Controlled Trial

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Low Health Literacy
recommendation_text: Use the 'chunk and check' method when providing complex information: 1) Break information into small, manageable chunks 2) Present one chunk at a time 3) Check understanding before moving to the next chunk by asking 'What questions do you have about what I just explained?' Document areas requiring additional explanation.
implementation_guidance: Implement for all patient education, particularly for complex treatment plans or procedures. Use plain language (6th grade level or below). Supplement verbal information with visual aids when possible.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient comprehension of health information, increased adherence to treatment plans, and reduced errors in self-management.
target_population: All patients, particularly those with limited health literacy, limited English proficiency, or cognitive impairment
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant improvement in treatment adherence and outcomes.
citation_authors: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Frailty
recommendation_text: Perform the FRAIL scale assessment by asking about: F (Fatigue) - 'Are you fatigued?' R (Resistance) - 'Can you climb one flight of stairs?' A (Ambulation) - 'Can you walk one block?' I (Illnesses) - 'Do you have more than 5 illnesses?' L (Loss of weight) - 'Have you lost more than 5% of weight in the past 6 months?' Score 1 point for each 'yes' to F, I, L or 'no' to R, A. Implement comprehensive geriatric assessment for scores ≥3.
implementation_guidance: Screen annually for all patients 65+ or those with multiple chronic conditions. Document scores in a dedicated section of the EHR. Develop referral pathways for physical therapy, nutrition, and geriatric consultation based on results.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 15-20% more frail patients, earlier intervention to prevent functional decline, and reduced hospitalizations and falls.
target_population: Adults 65+ and younger patients with multiple chronic conditions or functional limitations
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant reduction in healthcare utilization and institutional care costs.
citation_authors: Morley JE, Malmstrom TK, Miller DK
citation_title: A simple frailty questionnaire (FRAIL) predicts outcomes in middle aged African Americans

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Cost Concerns
recommendation_text: When patients express medication cost concerns, take these specific actions: 1) Review current medications for potential generic substitutions 2) Check for therapeutic alternatives in lower cost tiers 3) Investigate patient assistance programs 4) Consider 90-day supplies to reduce copays 5) Document interventions in the EHR and follow up within 2 weeks to ensure medication access.
implementation_guidance: Train staff to identify cost concern cues. Create a resource list of patient assistance programs. Develop protocols for pharmacist consultation when cost barriers are identified. Document cost-related interventions in a consistent location.
expected_outcomes: 25-30% reduction in cost-related medication non-adherence, improved affordability of prescribed regimens, and better chronic disease control.
target_population: Patients expressing medication cost concerns, those with high out-of-pocket costs, and those with multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant improvement in medication adherence and disease outcomes.
citation_authors: Viswanathan M, Golin CE, Jones CD, et al.
citation_title: Interventions to Improve Adherence to Self-administered Medications for Chronic Diseases in the United States: A Systematic Review

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Caregiver Strain
recommendation_text: Use the Modified Caregiver Strain Index by asking caregivers 13 specific yes/no questions about: sleep disruption, inconvenience, physical strain, confinement, family adjustments, changes in personal plans, emotional adjustments, upsetting behaviors, time demands, and feelings of being overwhelmed. Score 1 point for each 'yes' and provide immediate support resources for scores ≥7.
implementation_guidance: Assess at least annually for all primary caregivers. Create a private setting for assessment. Develop a resource list of caregiver support services. Document scores and referrals provided.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30-40% more caregivers experiencing significant strain, increased referrals to support services, and reduced caregiver burnout.
target_population: Family caregivers of patients with chronic conditions, disabilities, or cognitive impairment
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant impact on caregiver health and patient care quality.
citation_title: Analysis of the reliability of the Modified Caregiver Strain Index
citation_journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series B

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Depression
recommendation_text: For patients prescribed antidepressants, implement these specific strategies: 1) Explain that full benefits may take 2-4 weeks 2) Discuss specific side effects to expect and how long they typically last 3) Schedule follow-up at 2 weeks to assess side effects 4) Use reminder systems tailored to patient preference 5) Document adherence barriers and interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement at initial prescription and reinforce at follow-up visits. Provide both verbal and written information. Create a follow-up system to check in with patients within the first week of starting medication. Document specific barriers identified and strategies implemented.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% improvement in antidepressant adherence at 3 months, reduced premature discontinuation, and improved depression outcomes.
target_population: Patients newly prescribed antidepressant medications or those with history of non-adherence
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant improvement in depression outcomes and reduced healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Fortney JC, Pyne JM, Edlund MJ, et al.
citation_title: A randomized trial of telemedicine-based collaborative care for depression

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Nutrition Risk
recommendation_text: Use the DETERMINE checklist to assess nutrition risk by asking about: Disease, Eating poorly, Tooth loss/mouth pain, Economic hardship, Reduced social contact, Multiple medications, Involuntary weight loss/gain, Needs assistance in self-care, and Elder years above 80. Score 1 point for each risk factor present and implement nutrition intervention for scores ≥3.
implementation_guidance: Screen annually for all older adults and those with chronic conditions. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop referral pathways to dietitians, food assistance programs, and meal delivery services based on identified risks.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 20-25% more patients with nutrition risk, increased appropriate referrals to nutrition services, and improved nutritional status.
target_population: Older adults, those with chronic conditions affecting nutrition, and those with recent weight changes
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant impact on health outcomes and functional status.
citation_authors: Posner BM, Jette AM, Smith KW, Miller DR
citation_title: Nutrition and health risks in the elderly: the nutrition screening initiative

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Sleep Quality
recommendation_text: Ask patients these specific questions about sleep: 1) 'How long does it typically take you to fall asleep?' 2) 'How many times do you wake up during the night?' 3) 'How many hours of sleep do you get each night?' 4) 'Do you feel rested when you wake up?' 5) 'Does poor sleep affect your daily activities?' Document responses and implement sleep hygiene education for identified problems.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate questions into routine health assessments. Create a sleep hygiene handout with specific recommendations. Document sleep patterns and interventions in the EHR. Consider referral to sleep specialist for patients with significant disruption.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30-40% more patients with sleep disorders, improved sleep quality through non-pharmacological interventions, and reduced inappropriate use of sleep medications.
target_population: All adult patients, particularly those with chronic conditions, mental health disorders, or complaints of fatigue
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for improved quality of life and reduced healthcare utilization.
citation_title: Sleep Health: Can We Define It? Does It Matter?

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Chronic Pain
recommendation_text: Implement the 4 A's approach for chronic pain management: 1) Analgesia - Ask 'On a scale of 0-10, how would you rate your pain before and after taking medication?' 2) Activities - Ask 'What activities can you do when your pain is controlled?' 3) Adverse effects - Ask 'What side effects are you experiencing from pain medications?' 4) Aberrant behaviors - Monitor for concerning patterns. Document all four components at each visit.
implementation_guidance: Use at every visit for patients with chronic pain. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop clear protocols for addressing concerning findings. Schedule regular reassessment of pain management effectiveness.
expected_outcomes: More comprehensive assessment of pain treatment effectiveness, improved functional outcomes, and earlier identification of medication-related problems.
target_population: Patients with chronic pain conditions, particularly those on long-term pain medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for improved pain management and reduced complications from pain treatments.
citation_title: Managing chronic nonmalignant pain: overcoming obstacles to the use of opioids
